source: notebooks/colab/paper/paper_scale_real_jepa.ipynb, executed in Colab. Values copied from its printed output in results/paper_scale_output.txt; the figure is results/figures/paper_scale.png.

setup.images: First 200 images of the CIFAR-100 test set, 32x32, resized to 224x224 (bilinear) before encoding; mean-pooled over patches
setup.replay: normalised: unit-length embeddings in F(a); the diffusion graph also uses cosine similarity

verdict_printed: Does the balanced regime hold with real embeddings? YES — decay rate predicts survival/ranking
notes: The notebook's YES comes from the test rho > 0.5 alone; it doesn't look at survivors, and there are none.
The top ten are equal to the six printed decimals, so their order comes from differences smaller than 0.000001.
The closing 'Paper's setup / Paper's result' lines are text written into the notebook, not computed.

Summing the equation over all memories, diffusion drops out (the graph is symmetric) and the replay weights add up to 1: d(sum a)/dt = -sum(alpha_i a_i) - delta*N*sum(a) + eta*S(t). With N = 200 and delta = 0.1, inhibition is 20 per unit of total activation, against decay of 0.5 to 1.5.

From that equation, the long-run time average of the total is about eta*p/(mean alpha + delta*N) = 0.24/21 = 0.0114, about 0.000057 per memory; with replay at every step it could not stay above about 0.8/21/200 = 0.00019 per memory. All 200 above 0.001 needs a total of 0.2.
Replay entropy is not printed; the figure shows it at its maximum, ln 200 = 5.30, i.e. replay spread evenly.
